title: Shell structure in half-lives: ${}^3\mathrm{H}$ and ${}^{14}\mathrm{C}$ as worked examples
html:
The shell correction conjecture (Skein shell correction) explains transition rates based on the Skein polynomial factorization of parent and daughter links.

Example 1: Tritium {}^{3}\mathrm{H} \to {}^{3}\mathrm{He}

Superallowed character (\log ft = 3.05). The parent (1, 2) and daughter (2, 1) are mirror nuclei. q \leftrightarrow q^{-1} conjugation relates their Skein polynomials. For mirror pairs, q-conjugation maps \hat{V}_i(q) \mapsto \hat{V}_i(q^{-1}), yielding a maximum overlap |q/q^{-1}|^2 = q^4 per affected generator.

Result. The categorical computation predicts t_{1/2} \approx 12.4 yr versus observed 12.3 yr. The shell correction is 0.

Example 2: Carbon-14 {}^{14}\mathrm{C} \to {}^{14}\mathrm{N}

Parent link. The 8 neutrons form a closed sub-link. The Skein polynomial factors: J_{8\mathfrak{n}}(q) = J_{\mathcal{N}(0,2)}(q)^4 \cdot (\text{linking factors}).

Daughter link. The daughter n = 7 is not magic. The neutron shell is broken.

Anomalous slowness (\log ft = 9.04). Beta decay must break a closed sub-link. The matrix element measures overlap between a factorized and non-factorized state, suppressing the overlap by |J_{\mathcal{N}(0,2)}(q)|. This yields |\mathcal{M}|^2 \sim 10^{-6}.

The 17% residual. The leading-order prediction (6690 yr) overestimates the observed 5730 yr. The shell correction increases \mathfrak{Q}_\beta, accelerating decay.

Summary

See Table.

Transitions altering a closed sub-link suffer the largest corrections. The shell correction emerges from the discrete structure of the Skein polynomial.
